steps.cap: Dose 1 gives C0 = 40 mg/L. Eight hours is two half-lives of 4 hr, so 40 falls to 10 mg/L just before dose 2.
Dose 2 adds another 40 mg/L to the 10 still present: 50.0 mg/L, which falls to 12.5 mg/L by 16 hr.
Each dose adds 40 mg/L to a larger remainder, so the peaks climb 40.0, 50.0, 52.5, 53.1, 53.3, 53.3 mg/L and stop climbing.

The climb is over within 3 to 5 half-lives, 12 to 20 hours. At steady state the curve repeats between Cmax 53.3 and Cmin 13.3 mg/L; the average, 28.9 mg/L, sits below the midpoint 33.3 because the curve spends more of each interval at the lower concentrations.
After the sixth dose the level falls by first-order elimination alone, halving every 4 hours.

md_bolus_steps.title: Repeated IV bolus, dose by dose

steps.cap: From 0 to 2 hr the first infusion runs: C = (R/(VD k))(1 − e^−kt) with t = 2 hr gives 17.28 mg/L.
With the infusion off, the level falls first order from 17.28: at 6 hr it is 17.28 × e^(−0.6) = 9.48 mg/L.
The second infusion builds exactly as the first did, to 17.28 mg/L at 8 hr. The leftover of dose 1 has fallen to 7.03 mg/L, so the plasma level at 8 hr is 24.30 mg/L.
At 12 hr dose 1 has declined 10 hr and gives 3.86 mg/L; dose 2 has declined 4 hr and gives 9.48 mg/L. The plasma concentration is the sum, 13.34 mg/L.
